You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Headline view:** The Seller's package is not "fair and balanced". It combines a tight liability regime with a disclosure/knowledge construct that would, in practice, defeat most Warranty Claims, while leaving three pre-Completion value items (Riverlark debt, closing bonuses, Ironquay IP) sitting with the Buyer after Completion. Several Seller Update statements are also contradicted by the Seller's own Disclosure Letter. Below I set out the issues in order of economic significance, then my recommended mark-up positions.

---

## A. The three "money" items – these are not negotiating points, they are deal mechanics

### 1. Riverlark Bank facility (~AUD 3.2m) – release "following Completion" (Cl 2/7)
- The deal is debt-free/cash-free. A release *after* Completion means the Buyer acquires a company carrying AUD 3.2m of bank debt, almost certainly secured over all assets (and probably the shares). The facility also has a change-of-control clause (DD-003 cl 8.1) – Completion itself will be an event of default unless the lender consents or is repaid.
- The Disclosure Letter (item 3) confirms the facility is **not repaid and no discharge is in the data room**, which contradicts the Seller Update's "will be addressed".
- **Position:** Repayment at Completion out of the purchase price, via a payout letter from Riverlark delivered pre-Completion specifying the exact figure (principal, interest, break costs). Completion deliverables to include executed deeds of release/discharge of all security and PPSR release/discharge authorisations. Any amount not repaid is a deduction from the price. No Completion without it.

### 2. DD-005 closing bonuses (AUD 420,000) – "a matter for the Seller", not in funds flow
- These are triggered by Completion. If they are not itemised in the funds flow, they will in practice be paid by Paperbark (i.e., by the Buyer) after Completion. "Continued-employment conditions" make this worse – the trigger date may fall post-Completion, when the Seller is gone.
- Gross cost is higher than AUD 420k: superannuation guarantee (12%), NSW payroll tax (~5.45%), PAYG withholding mechanics. The Seller's own disclosure says it does not address on-costs.
- **Position:** Treat the bonuses *plus all on-costs* as a Transaction Cost / Debt-like Item deducted from the price in the funds flow, or paid by the Seller through Company payroll pre-Completion and reimbursed. Specific indemnity for any shortfall. Confirm no other change-of-control / retention / acceleration triggers (options, STI/LTI, notice entitlements) exist.

### 3. Ironquay Development Studio – IP title gap (Cl 11.1)
- DD-004 cl 7.3: title to SOW3 Project Materials transfers only on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180k open. Until paid, Paperbark **does not own** the IP – Ironquay does. If that code or material is embedded in the product, this is an ownership defect in the core asset, not a AUD 180k accounts-payable issue.
- An indemnity "limited to the SOW3 payment" covers the wrong risk. It doesn't cover: Ironquay refusing to assign, licensing/third-party claims, injunction or re-development costs, customer claims, or loss of sale value.
- **Position:** (i) Condition precedent / Completion deliverable: evidence of cleared payment *and* an executed confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay in agreed form; (ii) if not delivered, specific indemnity for all Loss arising from any failure of Paperbark to own or have unrestricted rights to the Project Materials, capped at the purchase price, outside basket/de minimis, 6-year claim period; (iii) warranty that no other supplier contract has a payment-conditional IP transfer.

---

## B. The liability regime – designed so that very little is ever recoverable

### 4. Fundamental / title warranties under the general cap and time limits
- Capping title and capacity at 20% / 18 months is far outside market and unacceptable. If the Seller does not own the shares, the Buyer has lost 100% of the price, not 20%.
- **Position:** Title, capacity, authority (and no-insolvency) warranties: cap = 100% of price; claim period = 6 years (contractual limitation in NSW) or 7 years. Also uncapped for fraud, dishonesty or wilful concealment.

### 5. Tax and IP "settled under the general regime"
- **Tax:** 18 months is shorter than the ATO's standard 4-year amendment period (longer for complex matters, unlimited for fraud/evasion). Tax warranties and a separate tax indemnity should run 7 years, capped at the price, with the indemnity outside basket/de minimis.
- **IP:** given the Ironquay gap, IP warranties should attract an enhanced cap (at least 50% of price; we'd open at 100%) and 3-year period, and the specific indemnity in item 3 must sit outside the general regime.

### 6. General cap 20% / 18 months (Cl 12.1, 12.3)
- 20% on a AUD 24m deal is at the low end but within range; 18 months is short. The real problem is the combination with items 7–10 below. Open at 50% / 24–36 months and trade towards 25–30% / 24 months, provided the carve-outs are secured.
- Also consider **W&I insurance** or a **retention/escrow** (c. 10% for 18–24 months). Harbourglass is a "Ventures" vehicle – we should assess its covenant strength and seek a parent/principal guarantee if it will distribute proceeds.

### 7. "Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (Cl 12.3/13) and "limitations apply to all Claims of any nature" (Cl 9.3/12.8/20.5)
- This drags **indemnities, covenants, leakage, completion accounts adjustments, Riverlark/bonus deductions, Ironquay and privacy indemnities, and tax** inside the 20% / 18-month / basket regime. It also purports to exclude or limit fraud and statutory misleading-or-deceptive-conduct claims. Under Australian law you cannot contract out of ACL s 18 / ASIC Act s 12DA, but a broad non-reliance clause will be run against us on causation, so we should not concede it.
- **Position:** Reverse the default: limitations apply *only* to Warranty Claims and *only* where expressly stated. Express carve-outs for: fraud, dishonesty, wilful concealment; fundamental warranties; tax; specific indemnities; leakage; price adjustment and funds-flow deductions; Seller covenants (restraint, confidentiality); and anything the Seller is obliged to do at Completion. Non-reliance to be mutual-reasonable and not apply to fraud or to statements in the SPA/Disclosure Letter.

### 8. De minimis AUD 25k / deductible basket AUD 250k (Cl 12.2)
- The basket is a *deductible* ("only the excess"), not a tipping basket. With a AUD 25k per-claim floor, a pattern of mid-size problems is unrecoverable.
- Note the Sandbar renewals: three "related" renewals of exactly AUD 110k each. Whether or not deliberate, splitting invites arguments about separate claims and thresholds.
- **Position:** De minimis AUD 10–15k; tipping basket at ~0.5–1% (AUD 120–240k); related claims and claims arising from the same facts aggregated for both thresholds; thresholds not applicable to fundamental, tax, or indemnity claims.

### 9. Disclosure – general disclosure of entire data room and public registers (Sch 7; DL [1.1]–[1.2])
- Wholesale disclosure of "every fact ... in the data room" plus publicly searchable records (ASIC, PPSR, courts, IP registers, titles) means the Seller is effectively not giving warranties at all. Combined with [1.4] (no admission that anything is required) the Buyer is left to work out the problems itself.
- The data room cut-off is **22 September 2026** – six weeks stale today and will be more so at signing/Completion.
- **Position:** Disclosure effective only if **fairly disclosed** – i.e., in the Disclosure Letter, with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature, scope and likely financial impact. Data room disclosed only if indexed, provided to the Buyer by a specified date (not later than 5 business days pre-signing) and on a USB/locked copy annexed. No general disclosure of public registers (or limited to ASIC company extract and PPSR search of the Company dated within 5 days of signing). Updated disclosure at Completion permitted only for post-signing matters, with a Buyer right to terminate/claim for material new disclosures.

### 10. Buyer knowledge – including anything "discoverable" from data room/public records (Cl 8.3)
- This is a constructive-knowledge anti-sandbagging clause. It converts every item in the data room (and every public record) into an un-claimable matter, duplicating item 9 and swallowing the warranties. It also lets the Seller argue after the event that something was "discoverable".
- **Position:** Delete. Fall-back: limited to the *actual* knowledge of a named list of three or four Buyer deal-team individuals, having made no enquiry, of matters that would reasonably be understood as a breach – and never applicable to fundamental warranties, tax or indemnities. Pair with an express pro-sandbagging clause: Buyer's knowledge does not reduce or extinguish any Claim save as above.

---

## C. Conditions and operational risk items

### 11. Bluefen change-of-control consent – ~30% of revenue (Cl 3/6.3)
- DD-002: cl 11.2 consent, with conditions in cl 11.3. Disclosure Letter item 2 confirms **no consent and no evidence the conditions are satisfied** – again contradicting "is addressed". A "reasonable endeavours" obligation is weak and "satisfied on delivery of written consent" ignores the cl 11.3 conditions and any consent given on terms adverse to Paperbark (price concessions, extended terms, termination rights).
- **Position:** Condition precedent: Bluefen's written consent, **unconditional or on terms approved by the Buyer**, with the cl 11.3 conditions evidenced as satisfied, and no amendment to the Bluefen contract without Buyer consent. Seller to use *all reasonable endeavours*; Buyer-only right to waive; long-stop date; termination right. Consider a price adjustment or deferred/escrowed consideration (e.g., AUD 2–3m) if consent is obtained on adverse terms or Bluefen terminates within 12 months.

### 12. DD-006 export/privacy incident
- ~1,240 records of names, business emails, roles and activity timestamps sent to an unintended external recipient. That is personal information under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth). The Seller's "preliminary operational matter" framing is self-serving: the NDB scheme requires a 30-day assessment; the incident is already more than six weeks old with no stated conclusion. Customer contracts (Bluefen especially) may contain their own notification obligations. Civil penalty exposure for serious/repeated interferences is now significant, and reputational exposure to a data-analytics business is obvious.
- **Position:** Pre-signing: Seller to complete the assessment, produce the report, confirm whether recipient accessed/deleted the file, and confirm position on OAIC and customer notification. SPA: specific indemnity for all Loss (including regulatory penalties, notification costs, customer claims, remediation), outside basket/de minimis, capped at the price, 4-year claim period; conduct-of-claims rights for the Buyer; warranty that no other incidents exist; covenant to notify and consult pre-Completion.

### 13. Sandbar renewals – AUD 330k (DD-008/DD-011)
- Three "related" renewals of AUD 110k each, which the Seller labels "ordinary course" while its own letter admits it does not know whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued. Request the contracts and confirm (i) whether they are genuinely needed, (ii) whether committed pre- or post-signing (interim covenant consent threshold), (iii) whether accrued (debt-like item). Any non-ordinary commitment between signing and Completion requires Buyer consent; aggregate for all thresholds.

### 14. Title to shares (DD-012)
- The Seller relies solely on the share register and expressly says the Buyer has not verified. The register is prima facie evidence only. Buyer must obtain: current ASIC extract, constitution, share certificates (or confirmation none issued), PPSR search of the Company and of Harbourglass (Riverlark may hold security over the shares), confirmation of no options/convertible instruments/shareholder agreements or trusts. Title warranty must be fundamental and uncapped (item 4).

### 15. Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009) – lower priority
- Lease: confirm whether a change in control of the tenant is deemed an assignment (common in NSW commercial leases). If only notification, make it a pre-Completion Seller obligation with evidence delivered at Completion.
- Mossvale: assignment restriction only; confirm no change-of-control definition. Warranty that no other material contract has a change-of-control trigger beyond Bluefen and Riverlark.

---

## D. Internal inconsistencies to put to the Seller
1. Seller Update says Bluefen is "addressed" / Riverlark "will be addressed"; Disclosure Letter items 2 and 3 confirm neither has happened.
2. Seller Update says bonuses are "a matter for the Seller"; Disclosure Letter item 5 confirms they are *not* in the funds flow – i.e., no mechanism exists for the Seller to bear them.
3. Seller Update says Ironquay indemnity is "adequate"; Disclosure Letter item 4 confirms no receipt of payment and no assignment exists.
4. Seller Update says DD-006 is "not expected to be material"; Disclosure Letter item 6 confirms the investigation is incomplete and scope unknown.

These should be called out in the cover note – they go to the credibility of the Seller's "fair and balanced" framing and support a firm mark-up.

---

## E. Summary of recommended positions

| # | Issue | Seller position | Buyer position |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Riverlark AUD 3.2m | Release post-Completion | Repaid at Completion from price; payout letter, releases, PPSR discharges as deliverables |
| 2 | Closing bonuses AUD 420k | Not in funds flow | Deduct bonuses + on-costs from price; specific indemnity |
| 3 | Ironquay IP | Indemnity capped at SOW3 payment | CP/deliverable: payment + confirmatory assignment; indemnity for all IP loss, cap = price |
| 4 | Fundamental/title | Same as general | Cap = price; 6–7 years; uncapped for fraud |
| 5 | Tax / IP | General regime | Tax: 7 yrs, cap = price, indemnity. IP: enhanced cap, 3 yrs |
| 6 | General cap/period | 20% / 18 months | Open 50% / 24–36 months; settle ~25–30% / 24 months; W&I or 10% retention; guarantor |
| 7 | Limitations apply to all Claims | Yes | Only Warranty Claims; express carve-outs (fraud, fundamental, tax, indemnities, leakage, adjustments) |
| 8 | Thresholds | 25k / 250k deductible | 10–15k / tipping basket ~AUD 120–240k; aggregation; n/a to fundamental/tax/indemnities |
| 9 | Disclosure | Whole data room + public registers | Fair disclosure standard; indexed annexed data room; no general public-record disclosure |
| 10 | Buyer knowledge | Constructive, incl. "discoverable" | Delete; fall-back actual knowledge of named individuals; pro-sandbagging clause |
| 11 | Bluefen consent | Reasonable endeavours; written consent suffices | CP: unconditional/Buyer-approved consent + cl 11.3 satisfied; all reasonable endeavours; long-stop; price protection |
| 12 | Privacy incident | "Not material" | Complete assessment pre-signing; specific indemnity outside thresholds; conduct rights |
| 13 | Sandbar AUD 330k | Ordinary course | Produce contracts; interim covenant consent; aggregate; debt-like if accrued |
| 14 | Title | Share register only | Independent verification; fundamental warranty |
| 15 | Lease / Mossvale | Notification only / no consent | Confirm no deemed assignment; Seller to give notice pre-Completion; broad CoC warranty |

**Suggested priority for the mark-up call:** items 1–3 (non-negotiable mechanics), then 4, 7, 9, 10 (the regime), then 11–12 (conditions/indemnities), then commercial trading on 6 and 8.

Two caveats: I have worked only from the Seller's summary and Disclosure Letter, not the underlying DD documents or the SPA draft itself, so clause references and the Ironquay/Bluefen analysis should be confirmed against the source documents; and this is deal-team analysis to be settled with the Buyer's instructing solicitors before it goes to the other side.
=== END ADVICE ===
